tools.name: search_cards
tools.description: Use this first when the user names a trading card and wants its value, price, or whether to grade it. Searches 1.5M+ Pokémon, Magic, Yu-Gi-Oh!, One Piece, Lorcana, sports (baseball, basketball, football, hockey, soccer, wrestling, UFC and more) and entertainment cards by name, set, number and year, returning ungraded and PSA 10 market prices in USD from real sold listings. Returns card ids for get_card_prices, grading_roi and get_price_history. Do not use for sealed product, for cards you already have an id for, or for price prediction.

query.description: Card name, optionally with set, number or year. Examples: "Umbreon VMAX Evolving Skies", "1986 Fleer Jordan", "Charizard base set 4/102".

game.description: Restrict to one game or sport. Omit when unsure.

set_id.description: Expansion id from list_sets, to search inside one set.

limit.description: How many matches to return, best match first (1 to 50, default 10).

tools.name: get_card_prices
tools.description: Use this when the user wants the full current value of a specific card: ungraded prices by condition (NM/LP/MP/HP) and graded prices for every company and grade on record (PSA, CGC, BGS, SGC, TAG). Requires a card id from search_cards. Prices are USD market values from real sold listings, refreshed daily. Do not use to search by name.

card_id.description: Catalog card id from search_cards, e.g. "swsh7-215" or "pricecharting-1821843".

tools.name: grading_roi
tools.description: Use this when the user asks whether a card is worth grading, submitting to PSA/CGC/BGS/SGC/TAG, or what a PSA 10 adds. Returns raw vs PSA 9 vs PSA 10 market prices, the gem premium, net profit after grading fees per outcome, expected value by gem probability, the break-even gem rate, which company pays most, and a plain-language verdict. Requires a card id from search_cards. It does not assess the condition of the user's copy.

grading_fee_usd.description: Grading fee to assume. Defaults to a $25 economy tier; the table also shows $50 and $150.

tools.name: get_price_history
tools.description: Use this when the user asks how a card's price has changed over weeks or months, or wants a trend for the raw or a PSA-graded series. Returns dated USD market values for the last 7 to 180 days. Requires a card id from search_cards. Do not use for forecasts.

days.description: How many days back the series should go (7 to 180, default 90).

grade.description: PSA grade for a graded series, e.g. "10" or "9". Omit for the raw (ungraded) series.

tools.name: best_cards_to_grade
tools.description: Use this when the user asks which cards in a game, sport or set have the biggest payoff from grading. Ranks priced cards by expected net profit at a 50% gem rate (half PSA 10, half PSA 9, minus raw and the fee), requiring both PSA 9 and PSA 10 prices so thin-market outliers are excluded. Returns card ids for grading_roi. Do not use for a single named card.

set_slug.description: Optional set slug (as used on /sets/<game>/<slug>) to rank inside one set.

grading_fee_usd.description: Grading fee to assume. Defaults to $25.

limit.description: How many cards to return, best expected profit first (1 to 50, default 12).

tools.name: trending_cards
tools.description: Use this when the user asks which cards are rising, hot, spiking, crashing or trending, in one game or across all games. Returns the biggest 30-day gainers (or drops) with the percentage change, measured on the PSA 10 price where the card has one and on the raw price otherwise; moves over 300% are excluded as bad data. Do not use for a single named card or for long-term history.

game.description: Restrict to one game or sport; omit for all.

min_market_usd.description: Ignore cards whose raw price is below this.

limit.description: How many cards to return, biggest move first (1 to 50, default 15).

tools.name: liquid_movers
tools.description: Use this when the user wants cards that are both rising in price and easy to sell: recent gainers filtered to cards with at least 25 recorded sales a year and a raw price of at least $5, across all games and sports. Better than trending_cards for flipping or selling decisions. Do not use for a single named card.

game.description: Restrict to one game or sport; omit for all.

include_unknown_volume.description: Also include cards whose yearly sales count is not tracked (mostly Pokémon from the Scrydex source). Off by default so every result has a verifiable sales figure.

limit.description: How many cards to return, biggest 30-day gain first (1 to 50, default 15).

tools.name: list_sets
tools.description: Use this to find the set id for a game or sport (e.g. "Evolving Skies", "2019 Panini Prizm") before calling get_set_cards, or when the user asks which sets exist. Newest first. Do not use to price a single card.

game.description: Game or sport whose sets to list, e.g. "pokemon", "magicthegathering" or "baseball".

query.description: Optional substring to filter set names, e.g. "evolving" or "2019 prizm".

limit.description: How many sets to return, newest first (1 to 100, default 30). Narrow with query when the set you want is older.

tools.name: get_set_cards
tools.description: Use this when the user wants the most valuable cards in a specific set or a priced checklist of a set. Requires a set id from list_sets. Returns raw and PSA 10 USD prices per card. Do not use for a single named card; use search_cards instead.

game.description: Game or sport the set belongs to, e.g. "pokemon" or "basketball". Use the same value you passed to list_sets.

limit.description: How many cards to return in the chosen order (1 to 100, default 25). total_cards in the result gives the full set size.
